text: From I-5 Exit 21 at Woodland, follow SR 503 east about 30 miles to Cougar. Continue east on Lewis River Road, which becomes Forest Road 90, to the Forest Road 83 junction, turn left and drive about 6 miles to the Marble Mountain Sno-Park, where the road is gated in winter and spring. A Washington Sno-Park permit is required December through March, and a Mount St. Helens climbing permit is required

From Trout Lake, drive north on Mt Adams Road to the FR 23 junction and bear right about a mile to the signed FR 80 turn for South Climb. Follow FR 80 for 3.7 miles to FR 8040, then FR 8040 for 8.1 miles to its end at the South Climb / Cold Springs trailhead; it is steep and narrow with sharp switchbacks, so no RVs or trailers. Self-issue a free wilderness permit at the trailhead, and buy the Casc

The approach starts from Bird Creek Meadows on the Yakama Nation side of the mountain, reached by the Mirror Lake road; the parking area sits at about 5,576-5,700 ft. You need a tribal-use permit for Tract D, bought at the fee station as you enter at the Mirror Lake gate — it cannot be obtained in advance, and it is only sold while the area is open to non-tribal use. The Yakama Nation sets that wi

From Cougar, follow FR-90, FR-83, FR-81 and Spur 830 to the Climbers Bivouac trailhead at 3,700 ft, the highest vehicle access on this side of the mountain. Ptarmigan Trail #216A starts from the parking area. A climbing permit is required year-round above 4,800 ft and is checked at or near the trailhead; permits sell on Recreation.gov and release on the 1st of the prior month. Climbers Bivouac and

Reached on Forest Roads 23, 21 and 2329 from the Randle or Trout Lake side. FR-2329 holds snow well into early summer, so check the road before committing — parties blocked short of the trailhead have had to walk or bushwhack an extra mile or more of road and forest to reach it.

From Randle on US 12, take Forest Road 23 south about 32 miles, the last stretch gravel, to FR 2329, then turn east past Takhlakh Lake about 5 miles to the trailhead. From Trout Lake, take Mt Adams Road and FR 23 north about 24 miles to the same junction. Roads are seasonal. A free wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead; a Mt. Adams climbing pass is needed above 7,000 ft May through Sep

From Packwood, drive US 12 west about 2.7 miles and turn left (south) on FS Road 21. Follow the gravel road about 13 miles, bear left onto FS Road 2150 toward Chambers Lake, and in under 3 miles turn right to the Snowgrass Flat Trailhead (Trail #96) at about 4,650 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or day fee is required, and a free Goat Rocks Wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

The trailhead sits at the end of Forest Road 2150, at about 4,600 feet, where the Snowgrass Flat Trail (#96) begins. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and a free self-issue Goat Rocks Wilderness permit is available at the trailhead kiosk. The access road has taken washout damage in past winters, so confirm current conditions before driving in.

pins.name: Conrad Meadows Trailhead (South Fork Tieton Trail #1120)

text: From US 12 at Rimrock Lake east of White Pass, take Tieton Road (FS Road 1200) to South Fork Tieton Road (FS Road 1000) and follow it about 12.6 miles, paved then good gravel, to the road end at Conrad Meadows, about 4,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or day fee is required to park, and a free Goat Rocks Wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

pins.name: Conrad Meadows / South Fork Tieton Trailhead (#1120)

text: From Naches, follow US 12 west about 22 miles and turn left onto Tieton Road (FR 1200). In 4.5 miles turn left onto South Fork Tieton Road (FR 1000) and follow it 12.6 miles to the trailhead at road's end in Conrad Meadows, about 4,050 ft; the last 7 miles are gravel. A day-use fee or annual recreation pass is required to park, plus a free self-issued Goat Rocks Wilderness permit.

pins.name: Eagle Peak Trailhead (Longmire, Nisqually Suspension Bridge)

text: From Ashford, follow SR 706 east to the park's Nisqually Entrance and continue about 6.5 miles to Longmire; a park entrance pass is required. Park at the lodge and museum lot, walk past the staff housing and cross the Nisqually River on the suspension bridge; the Eagle Peak trailhead is about 300 ft beyond the bridge on the east side of the river.

Drive SR 706 east through Ashford to the Nisqually Entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, then 6.5 miles on to Longmire. The road is paved and open essentially year round, conditions permitting. Park at Longmire and register at the Wilderness Information Center before you start.

From Ashford, follow SR 706 east through the Nisqually Entrance toward Paradise, turn right onto Stevens Canyon Road and drive about 3 miles, 1.5 miles past Reflection Lakes, to the Bench and Snow Lakes trailhead on the south side of the road. From the east, take Stevens Canyon Road west from SR 123. A park entrance pass is required; Stevens Canyon Road is closed by snow from fall to late spring.

From Ashford, follow SR 706 east through the Nisqually Entrance and drive about 15 miles toward Paradise to the Stevens Canyon Road junction; turn right and drive 1.5 miles to the Reflection Lakes parking. From the east, take Stevens Canyon Road west about 18 miles from SR 123. The Pinnacle Peak Trail starts on the south side of the road. A park entrance pass is required; in winter start from the

pins.name: Pinnacle Peak Trailhead (Reflection Lakes, Stevens Canyon Road)

text: From Ashford, follow SR 706 east through the Nisqually Entrance and drive about 15 miles toward Paradise to the Stevens Canyon Road junction; turn right and drive 1.5 miles to the Reflection Lakes parking. From the east, take Stevens Canyon Road west about 18 miles from SR 123. The trail starts on the south side of the road. A park entrance pass is required; when Stevens Canyon Road is snowed in,

Park at the Reflection Lakes pullouts on Stevens Canyon Road, at about 4,860 ft. It is a small paved pullout lot and it fills early on weekends, so plan an early arrival. A Mount Rainier National Park entrance fee applies, and there is no water at the lot, so fill up before you get here. The trail is signed but unnumbered and starts directly across Stevens Canyon Road from the parking. When the ro

Park at the Reflection Lakes pullouts on Stevens Canyon Road, about 1.4 miles east of the Paradise-Longmire Road junction and roughly 1.9 miles from the Paradise turnoff — an unpaved pullout on the south side of the road with room for about 35 cars, directly across from the largest of the Reflection Lakes. The signed trail for Pinnacle Peak/Plummer Peak starts right there; it's a maintained Mount

From Ashford, follow SR 706 east through the Nisqually Entrance and drive about 15 miles toward Paradise to the Stevens Canyon Road junction; turn right and drive 1.5 miles to the Reflection Lakes parking. From the east, take Stevens Canyon Road west about 18 miles from SR 123. The Pinnacle Peak Trail starts on the south side of the road. A park entrance pass is required; Stevens Canyon Road is cl

Drive the Paradise road (SR 706) inside Mount Rainier National Park to the Narada Falls pullout, just before the turnoff for the Paradise loop. This is the start to use while Stevens Canyon Road is snow-gated; when that road is open, roughly Memorial Day through mid-October, most parties park at the Reflection Lakes pullout instead and skip the first climb.

pins.name: West Side Road gate / Dry Creek Trailhead

text: From Ashford, follow SR 706 east to the Nisqually Entrance of Mount Rainier National Park. About 1 mile past the entrance, turn left onto Westside Road and follow the gravel road about 3 miles to the barricade at Dry Creek, where it closes to vehicles; park in the small lot south of it. The road to Dry Creek is open to vehicles only in summer, typically May to November, and a park entrance pass is

pins.name: West Side Road gate / Dry Creek Trailhead

text: From Ashford, follow SR 706 east to the park's Nisqually Entrance; a park entrance pass is required. About 1 mile past the entrance, turn left onto Westside Road and drive about 3 miles to the gate at the Dry Creek trailhead, near 2,900 ft, and park below the barricade. The road beyond is closed to vehicles, and the drivable section is open only in the summer season.

Drive SR 706 to Paradise, at about 5,400 ft; the highway is open year-round. The lot is large but fills by 9 AM in summer, so get there early. Entry requires a national park permit, and a park pass runs $30. The nearest supplies are in Ashford, about 25 miles away. In the winter season the climbing permit is self-registered at the old station kiosk at Paradise rather than at a staffed wilderness d

From SR 7 at Elbe, take SR 706 east through Ashford to the Nisqually Entrance, then follow the park road past Longmire to Paradise at about 5,400 ft, roughly 19 miles from the entrance. Overnight parking is allowed only in designated areas, and from November the road above Longmire is gated every night. A park entrance pass is required, plus a climbing permit for glacier travel or above 10,000 ft.

From SR 7 at Elbe, take SR 706 east through Ashford to the Nisqually Entrance, then follow the park road past Longmire to Paradise at about 5,400 ft, roughly 19 miles from the entrance. Overnight parking is allowed only in designated areas, and from November the road above Longmire is gated every night. A park entrance pass is required, plus a climbing permit for glacier travel or above 10,000 ft.
Paradise sits on the mountain's south side at about 5,400 ft, at the end of the Paradise road. The climb starts from the upper lot on the Skyline Trail.

From Enumclaw, drive SR 410 east about 43 miles to the White River Entrance, then follow White River Road about 3 miles to the parking area by the Fryingpan Creek bridge; the trail starts across the road. The road is open summer only. The Fryingpan Creek trailhead parking and its spur trail are closed while the park replaces the Fryingpan Creek Bridge, a project expected to run into late 2029; unt

pins.name: White River Campground / Glacier Basin Trailhead

text: From Enumclaw, WA-410 runs about 43 miles east to the park's White River entrance; turn onto the Sunrise Road, cross the White River and turn onto the White River Road, following it to the campground at the end. Sort the climbing permit and the route-specific briefing before you drive up — both are required for this line — and check the road, which is seasonal.

From Enumclaw, drive WA-410 east about 43 miles to the White River entrance of Mount Rainier National Park and turn right onto the Sunrise Road. After about 5 miles, cross the White River and turn left onto the White River Road, following it to its end at White River Campground; the Glacier Basin trailhead is at the upper end of the campground loop. A park entrance pass is required, and the road o

From Enumclaw, drive SR 410 east to the White River Entrance of the park and turn west onto the Sunrise Road. After about 5 miles, cross the White River and turn left onto the White River Campground road, following it to its end. Park in the day-hiking and climbing lot at about 4,300 ft; the trail starts in the campground's D loop. The road is open in summer only, and a park entrance pass is requi

Drive the Teanaway River Road to 29 Pines Campground, bear right where the pavement ends, then turn onto Stafford Creek Road and follow it a couple of miles to where it ends at the trailhead. The last stretch is dirt and washboarded but passable to low-clearance cars in dry conditions.

From I-90 Exit 85 east of Cle Elum, follow SR 970 about 7 miles and turn left onto Teanaway Road. Keep right onto North Fork Teanaway Road, which becomes gravel FR 9737 at 29 Pines Campground. Continue just under 4 miles and, just before the Beverly Creek bridge, turn right onto FR 9737-112, a rough one-lane spur best with high clearance, for about 1.4 miles to its end at about 3,650 ft.

Take I-90 to Exit 62 (Kachess Lake), turn left off the ramp and follow FR 49 (Kachess Lake Road) toward Kachess Lake. Follow the signs toward Lake Kachess Campground and turn left on FR 4930 (Box Canyon Road), which ends at a large lot and the Rachel Lake trailhead about 4 miles from the turn, around 2,800 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, plus a free self-issue wilderness permit.

From I-90 Exit 62, follow Kachess Lake Road to FS Road 4930 and drive it to the road end at about 2,800 ft. Trail #1313 leaves the parking area; a Northwest Forest Pass plus a self-issued wilderness permit are required at the board.

From I-90 Exit 80, drive through Roslyn and follow SR 903 north past Cle Elum Lake to Salmon La Sac, about 19 miles from Cle Elum. Just before the Salmon La Sac Campground entrance, turn right onto the gravel road to the Salmon La Sac trailhead, shared by the Waptus River and Cooper River trails. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and a self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit at the trail.
Take I-90 to Exit 47 and follow Denny Creek Road (FR 58) about 3 miles, past Denny Creek Campground, then turn left onto FR 5830 to the trailhead lot at about 2,300 feet.
Take I-90 Exit 47 and follow Denny Creek Road (Forest Road 58) up-valley to the large paved lot at about 2,280 ft.

From I-90 Exit 80, go north on Bullfrog Road to SR 903 and follow it through Roslyn and past Cle Elum Lake to Cooper Lake Road (FR 46), about 17 miles. Turn left on FR 46, pass the Cooper Lake turnoff and continue about 7 miles to Cooper Pass, then stay on the main road about 3 miles down to the signed Mineral Creek trailhead in the valley. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required t

From Cle Elum, drive Highway 903 north about 17 miles, past Lake Cle Elum, and turn left onto Cooper Lake Road (FR 4600). Follow FR 4600 about 7 miles, past the Cooper Lake turnoff, to Cooper Pass. Stay on the main road about 3 miles down to the small signed Mineral Creek trailhead in the valley bottom, at about 2,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

From I-90 Exit 85, take SR 970 east about 7 miles and turn left onto Teanaway Road. Follow it north as it becomes the North Fork Teanaway Road to the end of pavement at 29 Pines Campground, then continue straight on gravel FR 9737 for about 8.5 miles and take the left fork into the De Roux campground and trailhead, about a mile short of the road end. From I-90 Exit 85, take SR 970 east about 7 miles and turn left onto Teanaway Road. After 7.1 miles bear right onto North Fork Teanaway Road, and where the pavement ends keep right onto Forest Road 9737.
